# PocketBase JavaScript API

What every PocketOne app's `pb_hooks` and page code get from core, before any extension adds its own: the globals (`$app` and the `$`-helpers), the hooks, the functions and the classes. Types link to their pages, one per Go namespace ([core](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/core), [dbx](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/dbx), [router](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/router) and the [rest](/docs/reference/javascript#pocketbase)). Generated from PocketOne's `types.d.ts`, the same file your editor reads, so it matches the binary you run. Go names are written in JS form: Go's `FindRecordById` is `findRecordById`.

## Globals

### $app

```ts
$app: PocketBase
```

`$app` is the current running PocketBase instance that is globally
available in each .pb.js file.

_Note that this variable is available only in pb_hooks context._

Type: <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase#pocketbase">PocketBase</a></code>.

### $template

```ts
$template: template.Registry
```

`$template` is a global helper to load and cache HTML templates on the fly.

The templates uses the standard Go [html/template](https://pkg.go.dev/html/template)
and [text/template](https://pkg.go.dev/text/template) package syntax.

Example:

```js
const html = $template.loadFiles(
    "views/layout.html",
    "views/content.html",
).render({"name": "John"})
```

Type: <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/template#templateregistry">template.Registry</a></code>.

### console

```ts
console: Console
```

Writes to the app's log. @group PocketOne

Type: <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase#console">Console</a></code>.

### module

```ts
module: { exports: any; id: string; filename: string; loaded: boolean }
```

Inside a CommonJS module: the module. @group PocketOne

Type: <code>{ exports: any; id: string; filename: string; loaded: boolean }</code>.

### exports

```ts
exports: any
```

Inside a CommonJS module: `module.exports`. @group PocketOne

Type: <code>any</code>.

## $dbx

`$dbx` defines common utility for working with the DB abstraction.
For examples and guides please check the [Database guide](https://pocketbase.io/docs/js-database).

### $dbx.hashExp()

```ts
$dbx.hashExp(pairs: { [key:string]: any }): dbx.Expression
```

HashExp represents a hash expression.

A hash expression is a map whose keys are DB column names which need to be filtered according
to the corresponding values. For example, HashExp{"level": 2, "dept": 10} will generate
the SQL: "level"=2 AND "dept"=10.

HashExp also handles nil values and slice values. For example, HashExp{"level": []interface{}{1, 2}, "dept": nil}
will generate: "level" IN (1, 2) AND "dept" IS NULL.

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `pairs` | <code>{ [key:string]: any }</code> |

Returns <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/dbx#dbxexpression">dbx.Expression</a></code>.

### $dbx.in()

```ts
$dbx.in(col: string, ...values: { }[]): Expression
```

In generates an IN expression for the specified column and the list of allowed values.
If values is empty, a SQL "0=1" will be generated which represents a false expression.

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `col` | <code>string</code> |
| `...values` | <code>{ }[]</code> (optional) |

Returns <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/dbx#dbxexpression">Expression</a></code>.

### $dbx.exp()

```ts
$dbx.exp(e: string, ...params: Params[]): Expression
```

NewExp generates an expression with the specified SQL fragment and the optional binding parameters.

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `e` | <code>string</code> |
| `...params` | <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/dbx#dbxparams">Params</a>[]</code> (optional) |

Returns <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/dbx#dbxexpression">Expression</a></code>.

### $dbx.not()

```ts
$dbx.not(e: Expression): Expression
```

Not generates a NOT expression which prefixes "NOT" to the specified expression.

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `e` | <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/dbx#dbxexpression">Expression</a></code> |

Returns <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/dbx#dbxexpression">Expression</a></code>.

### $dbx.and()

```ts
$dbx.and(...exps: Expression[]): Expression
```

And generates an AND expression which concatenates the given expressions with "AND".

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `...exps` | <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/dbx#dbxexpression">Expression</a>[]</code> (optional) |

Returns <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/dbx#dbxexpression">Expression</a></code>.

### $dbx.or()

```ts
$dbx.or(...exps: Expression[]): Expression
```

Or generates an OR expression which concatenates the given expressions with "OR".

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `...exps` | <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/dbx#dbxexpression">Expression</a>[]</code> (optional) |

Returns <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/dbx#dbxexpression">Expression</a></code>.

### $dbx.notIn()

```ts
$dbx.notIn(col: string, ...values: { }[]): Expression
```

NotIn generates an NOT IN expression for the specified column and the list of disallowed values.
If values is empty, an empty string will be returned indicating a true expression.

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `col` | <code>string</code> |
| `...values` | <code>{ }[]</code> (optional) |

Returns <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/dbx#dbxexpression">Expression</a></code>.

### $dbx.like()

```ts
$dbx.like(col: string, ...values: string[]): (LikeExp)
```

Like generates a LIKE expression for the specified column and the possible strings that the column should be like.
If multiple values are present, the column should be like *all* of them. For example, Like("name", "key", "word")
will generate a SQL expression: "name" LIKE "%key%" AND "name" LIKE "%word%".

By default, each value will be surrounded by "%" to enable partial matching. If a value contains special characters
such as "%", "\", "_", they will also be properly escaped.

You may call Escape() and/or Match() to change the default behavior. For example, Like("name", "key").Match(false, true)
generates "name" LIKE "key%".

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `col` | <code>string</code> |
| `...values` | <code>string[]</code> (optional) |

Returns <code>(<a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/dbx#dbxlikeexp">LikeExp</a>)</code>.

### $dbx.orLike()

```ts
$dbx.orLike(col: string, ...values: string[]): (LikeExp)
```

OrLike generates an OR LIKE expression.
This is similar to Like() except that the column should be like one of the possible values.
For example, OrLike("name", "key", "word") will generate a SQL expression:
"name" LIKE "%key%" OR "name" LIKE "%word%". Please see Like() for more details.

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `col` | <code>string</code> |
| `...values` | <code>string[]</code> (optional) |

Returns <code>(<a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/dbx#dbxlikeexp">LikeExp</a>)</code>.

### $dbx.notLike()

```ts
$dbx.notLike(col: string, ...values: string[]): (LikeExp)
```

NotLike generates a NOT LIKE expression.
For example, NotLike("name", "key", "word") will generate a SQL expression:
"name" NOT LIKE "%key%" AND "name" NOT LIKE "%word%". Please see Like() for more details.

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `col` | <code>string</code> |
| `...values` | <code>string[]</code> (optional) |

Returns <code>(<a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/dbx#dbxlikeexp">LikeExp</a>)</code>.

### $dbx.orNotLike()

```ts
$dbx.orNotLike(col: string, ...values: string[]): (LikeExp)
```

OrNotLike generates an OR NOT LIKE expression.
For example, OrNotLike("name", "key", "word") will generate a SQL expression:
"name" NOT LIKE "%key%" OR "name" NOT LIKE "%word%". Please see Like() for more details.

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `col` | <code>string</code> |
| `...values` | <code>string[]</code> (optional) |

Returns <code>(<a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/dbx#dbxlikeexp">LikeExp</a>)</code>.

### $dbx.exists()

```ts
$dbx.exists(exp: Expression): Expression
```

Exists generates an EXISTS expression by prefixing "EXISTS" to the given expression.

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `exp` | <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/dbx#dbxexpression">Expression</a></code> |

Returns <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/dbx#dbxexpression">Expression</a></code>.

### $dbx.notExists()

```ts
$dbx.notExists(exp: Expression): Expression
```

NotExists generates an EXISTS expression by prefixing "NOT EXISTS" to the given expression.

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `exp` | <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/dbx#dbxexpression">Expression</a></code> |

Returns <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/dbx#dbxexpression">Expression</a></code>.

### $dbx.between()

```ts
$dbx.between(col: string, from: { }, to: { }): Expression
```

Between generates a BETWEEN expression.
For example, Between("age", 10, 30) generates: "age" BETWEEN 10 AND 30

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `col` | <code>string</code> |
| `from` | <code>{ }</code> |
| `to` | <code>{ }</code> |

Returns <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/dbx#dbxexpression">Expression</a></code>.

### $dbx.notBetween()

```ts
$dbx.notBetween(col: string, from: { }, to: { }): Expression
```

NotBetween generates a NOT BETWEEN expression.
For example, NotBetween("age", 10, 30) generates: "age" NOT BETWEEN 10 AND 30

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `col` | <code>string</code> |
| `from` | <code>{ }</code> |
| `to` | <code>{ }</code> |

Returns <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/dbx#dbxexpression">Expression</a></code>.

## $security

`$security` defines low level helpers for creating
and parsing JWTs, random string generation, AES encryption, etc.

### $security.randomString()

```ts
$security.randomString(length: number): string
```

RandomString generates a cryptographically random string with the specified length.

The generated string matches [A-Za-z0-9]+ and it's transparent to URL-encoding.

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `length` | <code>number</code> |

Returns <code>string</code>.

### $security.randomStringWithAlphabet()

```ts
$security.randomStringWithAlphabet(length: number, alphabet: string): string
```

RandomStringWithAlphabet generates a cryptographically random string
with the specified length and characters set.

It panics if for some reason rand.Int returns a non-nil error.

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `length` | <code>number</code> |
| `alphabet` | <code>string</code> |

Returns <code>string</code>.

### $security.randomStringByRegex()

```ts
$security.randomStringByRegex(pattern: string, ...optFlags: syntax.Flags[]): string
```

RandomStringByRegex generates a random string matching the regex pattern.
If optFlags is not set, fallbacks to `syntax.perl`.

NB! While the source of the randomness comes from [crypto/rand] this method
is not recommended to be used on its own in critical secure contexts because
the generated length could vary too much on the used pattern and may not be
as secure as simply calling `security.randomString`.
If you still insist on using it for such purposes, consider at least
a large enough minimum length for the generated string, e.g. `[a-z0-9]{30}`.

This function is inspired by github.com/pipe01/revregexp, github.com/lucasjones/reggen and other similar packages.

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `pattern` | <code>string</code> |
| `...optFlags` | <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/syntax#syntaxflags">syntax.Flags</a>[]</code> (optional) |

Returns <code>string</code>.

### $security.pseudorandomString()

```ts
$security.pseudorandomString(length: number): string
```

PseudorandomString generates a pseudorandom string with the specified length.

The generated string matches [A-Za-z0-9]+ and it's transparent to URL-encoding.

For a cryptographically random string (but a little bit slower) use RandomString instead.

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `length` | <code>number</code> |

Returns <code>string</code>.

### $security.pseudorandomStringWithAlphabet()

```ts
$security.pseudorandomStringWithAlphabet(length: number, alphabet: string): string
```

PseudorandomStringWithAlphabet generates a pseudorandom string
with the specified length and characters set.

For a cryptographically random (but a little bit slower) use RandomStringWithAlphabet instead.

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `length` | <code>number</code> |
| `alphabet` | <code>string</code> |

Returns <code>string</code>.

### $security.encrypt()

```ts
$security.encrypt(data: string|Array<number>, key: string): string
```

Encrypt encrypts "data" with the specified "key" (must be valid 32 char AES key).

This method uses AES-256-GCM block cypher mode.

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `data` | <code>string&#124;Array&lt;number&gt;</code> |
| `key` | <code>string</code> |

Returns <code>string</code>.

### $security.decrypt()

```ts
$security.decrypt(cipherText: string, key: string): string|Array<number>
```

Decrypt decrypts encrypted text with key (must be valid 32 chars AES key).

This method uses AES-256-GCM block cypher mode.

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `cipherText` | <code>string</code> |
| `key` | <code>string</code> |

Returns <code>string&#124;Array&lt;number&gt;</code>.

### $security.hs256()

```ts
$security.hs256(text: string, secret: string): string
```

HS256 creates a HMAC hash with sha256 digest algorithm.

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `text` | <code>string</code> |

Returns <code>string</code>.

```ts

```

HS512 creates a HMAC hash with sha512 digest algorithm.

| Parameter | Type |

| `text` | <code>string</code> |

Returns <code>string</code>.


Equal compares two hash strings for equality without leaking timing information.

SHA512 creates sha512 hash as defined in FIPS 180-4 from the provided text.

### $filesystem.fileFromURL()

```ts

```

fileFromURL creates a new File from the provided url by
downloading the resource and creating a BytesReader.

Example:

```js

// with custom timeout of 15sec
const file2 = $filesystem.fileFromURL("https://...", 15)
```

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `url` | <code>string</code> |
| `secTimeout` | <code>number</code> (optional) |

Returns <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/filesystem#filesystemfile">filesystem.File</a></code>.

## $filepath

`$filepath` defines common helpers for manipulating filename
paths in a way compatible with the target operating system-defined file paths.

### $filepath.base()

```ts
$filepath.base(path: string): string
```

Base returns the last element of path.
Trailing path separators are removed before extracting the last element.
If the path is empty, Base returns ".".
If the path consists entirely of separators, Base returns a single separator.

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `path` | <code>string</code> |

Returns <code>string</code>.

### $filepath.clean()

```ts
$filepath.clean(path: string): string
```

Clean returns the shortest path name equivalent to path
by purely lexical processing. It applies the following rules
iteratively until no further processing can be done:

 1. Replace multiple `Separator` elements with a single one.
 2. Eliminate each . path name element (the current directory).
 3. Eliminate each inner .. path name element (the parent directory)
```
    along with the non-.. element that precedes it.
```
 4. Eliminate .. elements that begin a rooted path:
```
    that is, replace "/.." by "/" at the beginning of a path,
    assuming Separator is '/'.
```

The returned path ends in a slash only if it represents a root directory,
such as "/" on Unix or `C:\` on Windows.

Finally, any occurrences of slash are replaced by Separator.

If the result of this process is an empty string, Clean
returns the string ".".

On Windows, Clean does not modify the volume name other than to replace
occurrences of "/" with `\`.
For example, Clean("//host/share/../x") returns `\\host\share\x`.

See also Rob Pike, “Lexical File Names in Plan 9 or
Getting Dot-Dot Right,”
https://9p.io/sys/doc/lexnames.html

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `path` | <code>string</code> |

Returns <code>string</code>.

### $filepath.dir()

```ts
$filepath.dir(path: string): string
```

Dir returns all but the last element of path, typically the path's directory.
After dropping the final element, Dir calls `Clean` on the path and trailing
slashes are removed.
If the path is empty, Dir returns ".".
If the path consists entirely of separators, Dir returns a single separator.
The returned path does not end in a separator unless it is the root directory.

On Windows, given a volume-only name such as "C:", Dir returns "C:.",
the current directory on drive C. To obtain the drive's root "C:\",
use `VolumeName` combined with a separator.

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `path` | <code>string</code> |

Returns <code>string</code>.

### $filepath.ext()

```ts
$filepath.ext(path: string): string
```

Ext returns the file name extension used by path.
The extension is the suffix beginning at the final dot
in the final element of path; it is empty if there is
no dot.

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `path` | <code>string</code> |

Returns <code>string</code>.

### $filepath.fromSlash()

```ts
$filepath.fromSlash(path: string): string
```

FromSlash returns the result of replacing each slash ('/') character
in path with a separator character. Multiple slashes are replaced
by multiple separators.

See also the Localize function, which converts a slash-separated path
as used by the io/fs package to an operating system path.

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `path` | <code>string</code> |

Returns <code>string</code>.

### $filepath.glob()

```ts
$filepath.glob(pattern: string): Array<string>
```

Glob returns the names of all files matching pattern or nil
if there is no matching file. The syntax of patterns is the same
as in `Match`. The pattern may describe hierarchical names such as
/usr/*\/bin/ed (assuming the `Separator` is '/').

Glob ignores file system errors such as I/O errors reading directories.
The only possible returned error is `ErrBadPattern`, when pattern
is malformed.

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `pattern` | <code>string</code> |

Returns <code>Array&lt;string&gt;</code>.

### $filepath.isAbs()

```ts
$filepath.isAbs(path: string): boolean
```

IsAbs reports whether the path is absolute.

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `path` | <code>string</code> |

Returns <code>boolean</code>.

### $filepath.join()

```ts
$filepath.join(...elem: string[]): string
```

Join joins any number of path elements into a single path,
separating them with an OS specific `Separator`. Empty elements
are ignored. The result is Cleaned. However, if the argument
list is empty or all its elements are empty, Join returns
an empty string.
On Windows, the result will only be a UNC path if the first
non-empty element is a UNC path.

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `...elem` | <code>string[]</code> (optional) |

Returns <code>string</code>.

### $filepath.match()

```ts
$filepath.match(pattern: string, name: string): boolean
```

Match reports whether name matches the shell file name pattern.
The pattern syntax is:

```
	pattern:
		{ term }
	term:
		'*'         matches any sequence of non-Separator characters
		'?'         matches any single non-Separator character
		'[' [ '^' ] { character-range } ']'
		            character class (must be non-empty)
		c           matches character c (c != '*', '?', '\\', '[')
		'\\' c      matches character c (except on Windows)

	character-range:
		c           matches character c (c != '\\', '-', ']')
		'\\' c      matches character c (except on Windows)
		lo '-' hi   matches character c for lo <= c <= hi
```

Path segments in the pattern must be separated by `Separator`.

Match requires pattern to match all of name, not just a substring.
The only possible returned error is `ErrBadPattern`, when pattern
is malformed.

On Windows, escaping is disabled. Instead, '\\' is treated as
path separator.

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `pattern` | <code>string</code> |
| `name` | <code>string</code> |

Returns <code>boolean</code>.

### $filepath.rel()

```ts
$filepath.rel(basePath: string, targPath: string): string
```

Rel returns a relative path that is lexically equivalent to targPath when
joined to basePath with an intervening separator. That is,
[Join](basePath, Rel(basePath, targPath)) is equivalent to targPath itself.

The returned path will always be relative to basePath, even if basePath and
targPath share no elements. Rel calls `Clean` on the result.

An error is returned if targPath can't be made relative to basePath
or if knowing the current working directory would be necessary to compute it.

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `basePath` | <code>string</code> |
| `targPath` | <code>string</code> |

Returns <code>string</code>.

### $filepath.split()

```ts
$filepath.split(path: string): [string, string]
```

Split splits path immediately following the final `Separator`,
separating it into a directory and file name component.
If there is no Separator in path, Split returns an empty dir
and file set to path.
The returned values have the property that path = dir+file.

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `path` | <code>string</code> |

Returns <code>[string, string]</code>.

### $filepath.splitList()

```ts
$filepath.splitList(path: string): Array<string>
```

SplitList splits a list of paths joined by the OS-specific `ListSeparator`,
usually found in PATH or GOPATH environment variables.
Unlike strings.Split, SplitList returns an empty slice when passed an empty
string.

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `path` | <code>string</code> |

Returns <code>Array&lt;string&gt;</code>.

### $filepath.toSlash()

```ts
$filepath.toSlash(path: string): string
```

ToSlash returns the result of replacing each separator character
in path with a slash ('/') character. Multiple separators are
replaced by multiple slashes.

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `path` | <code>string</code> |

Returns <code>string</code>.

### $filepath.walk()

```ts
$filepath.walk(root: string, fn: WalkFunc): void
```

Walk walks the file tree rooted at root, calling fn for each file or
directory in the tree, including root.

All errors that arise visiting files and directories are filtered by fn:
see the [`WalkFunc`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/filepath#filepathwalkfunc) documentation for details.

The files are walked in lexical order, which makes the output deterministic
but requires Walk to read an entire directory into memory before proceeding
to walk that directory.

Walk does not follow symbolic links.

Walk is less efficient than `WalkDir`, introduced in Go 1.16,
which avoids calling os.Lstat on every visited file or directory.

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `root` | <code>string</code> |
| `fn` | <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/filepath#filepathwalkfunc">WalkFunc</a></code> |

### $filepath.walkDir()

```ts
$filepath.walkDir(root: string, fn: fs.WalkDirFunc): void
```

WalkDir walks the file tree rooted at root, calling fn for each file or
directory in the tree, including root.

All errors that arise visiting files and directories are filtered by fn:
see the [`fs.walkDirFunc`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/fs#fswalkdirfunc) documentation for details.

The files are walked in lexical order, which makes the output deterministic
but requires WalkDir to read an entire directory into memory before proceeding
to walk that directory.

WalkDir does not follow symbolic links.

WalkDir calls fn with paths that use the separator character appropriate
for the operating system. This is unlike [io/fs.WalkDir], which always
uses slash separated paths.

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `root` | <code>string</code> |
| `fn` | <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/fs#fswalkdirfunc">fs.WalkDirFunc</a></code> |

## $os

`$os` defines common helpers for working with the OS level primitives
(eg. deleting directories, executing shell commands, etc.).

### $os.exec()

```ts
$os.exec(name: string, ...arg: string[]): (Cmd)
```

Legacy alias for $os.cmd().

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `name` | <code>string</code> |
| `...arg` | <code>string[]</code> (optional) |

Returns <code>(<a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/exec#execcmd">Cmd</a>)</code>.

### $os.cmd()

```ts
$os.cmd(name: string, ...arg: string[]): (Cmd)
```

Prepares an external OS command.

Example:

```js
// prepare the command to execute
const cmd = $os.cmd('ls', '-sl')

// execute the command and return its standard output as string
const output = toString(cmd.output());
```

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `name` | <code>string</code> |
| `...arg` | <code>string[]</code> (optional) |

Returns <code>(<a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/exec#execcmd">Cmd</a>)</code>.

### $os.args

```ts
$os.args: Array<string>
```

Args hold the command-line arguments, starting with the program name.

Returns <code>Array&lt;string&gt;</code>.

### $os.exit()

```ts
$os.exit(code: number): void
```

Exit causes the current program to exit with the given status code.
Conventionally, code zero indicates success, non-zero an error.
The program terminates immediately; deferred functions are not run.

For portability, the status code should be in the range [0, 125].

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `code` | <code>number</code> |

### $os.getenv()

```ts
$os.getenv(key: string): string
```

Getenv retrieves the value of the environment variable named by the key.
It returns the value, which will be empty if the variable is not present.
To distinguish between an empty value and an unset value, use `LookupEnv`.

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `key` | <code>string</code> |

Returns <code>string</code>.

### $os.dirFS()

```ts
$os.dirFS(dir: string): fs.FS
```

DirFS returns a file system (an fs.FS) for the tree of files rooted at the directory dir.

Note that DirFS("/prefix") only guarantees that the Open calls it makes to the
operating system will begin with "/prefix": DirFS("/prefix").Open("file") is the
same as os.Open("/prefix/file"). So if /prefix/file is a symbolic link pointing outside
the /prefix tree, then using DirFS does not stop the access any more than using
os.Open does. Additionally, the root of the fs.FS returned for a relative path,
DirFS("prefix"), will be affected by later calls to Chdir. DirFS is therefore not
a general substitute for a chroot-style security mechanism when the directory tree
contains arbitrary content.

Use [`Root.fS`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/os#osroot) to obtain a fs.FS that prevents escapes from the tree via symbolic links.

The directory dir must not be "".

The result implements [io/fs.StatFS], [io/fs.ReadFileFS], [io/fs.ReadDirFS], and
[io/fs.ReadLinkFS].

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `dir` | <code>string</code> |

Returns <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/fs#fsfs">fs.FS</a></code>.

### $os.readFile()

```ts
$os.readFile(name: string): string|Array<number>
```

ReadFile reads the named file and returns the contents.
A successful call returns err == nil, not err == EOF.
Because ReadFile reads the whole file, it does not treat an EOF from Read
as an error to be reported.
If there is an error, it will be of type [*PathError].

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `name` | <code>string</code> |

Returns <code>string&#124;Array&lt;number&gt;</code>.

### $os.writeFile()

```ts
$os.writeFile(name: string, data: string|Array<number>, perm: FileMode): void
```

WriteFile writes data to the named file, creating it if necessary.
If the file does not exist, WriteFile creates it with permissions perm (before umask);
otherwise WriteFile truncates it before writing, without changing permissions.
Since WriteFile requires multiple system calls to complete, a failure mid-operation
can leave the file in a partially written state.

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `name` | <code>string</code> |
| `data` | <code>string&#124;Array&lt;number&gt;</code> |
| `perm` | <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/os#osfilemode">FileMode</a></code> |

### $os.stat()

```ts
$os.stat(name: string): FileInfo
```

Stat returns a [`FileInfo`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/os#osfileinfo) describing the named file.
If there is an error, it will be of type [*PathError].

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `name` | <code>string</code> |

Returns <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/os#osfileinfo">FileInfo</a></code>.

### $os.readDir()

```ts
$os.readDir(name: string): Array<DirEntry>
```

ReadDir reads the named directory,
returning all its directory entries sorted by filename.
If an error occurs reading the directory,
ReadDir returns the entries it was able to read before the error,
along with the error.

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `name` | <code>string</code> |

Returns <code>Array&lt;<a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/os#osdirentry">DirEntry</a>&gt;</code>.

### $os.tempDir()

```ts
$os.tempDir(): string
```

TempDir returns the default directory to use for temporary files.

On Unix systems, it returns $TMPDIR if non-empty, else /tmp.
On Windows, it uses GetTempPath, returning the first non-empty
value from %TMP%, %TEMP%, %USERPROFILE%, or the Windows directory.
On Plan 9, it returns /tmp.

The directory is neither guaranteed to exist nor have accessible
permissions.

Returns <code>string</code>.

### $os.truncate()

```ts
$os.truncate(name: string, size: number): void
```

Truncate changes the size of the named file.
If the file is a symbolic link, it changes the size of the link's target.
If there is an error, it will be of type [*PathError].

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `name` | <code>string</code> |
| `size` | <code>number</code> |

### $os.getwd()

```ts
$os.getwd(): string
```

Getwd returns an absolute path name corresponding to the
current directory. If the current directory can be
reached via multiple paths (due to symbolic links),
Getwd may return any one of them.

On Unix platforms, if the environment variable PWD
provides an absolute name, and it is a name of the
current directory, it is returned.

Returns <code>string</code>.

### $os.mkdir()

```ts
$os.mkdir(name: string, perm: FileMode): void
```

Mkdir creates a new directory with the specified name and permission
bits (before umask).
If there is an error, it will be of type [*PathError].

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `name` | <code>string</code> |
| `perm` | <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/os#osfilemode">FileMode</a></code> |

### $os.mkdirAll()

```ts
$os.mkdirAll(path: string, perm: FileMode): void
```

MkdirAll creates a directory named path,
along with any necessary parents, and returns nil,
or else returns an error.
The permission bits perm (before umask) are used for all
directories that MkdirAll creates.
If path is already a directory, MkdirAll does nothing
and returns nil.

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `path` | <code>string</code> |
| `perm` | <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/os#osfilemode">FileMode</a></code> |

### $os.rename()

```ts
$os.rename(oldpath: string, newpath: string): void
```

Rename renames (moves) oldpath to newpath.
If newpath already exists and is not a directory, Rename replaces it.
If newpath already exists and is a directory, Rename returns an error.
OS-specific restrictions may apply when oldpath and newpath are in different directories.
Even within the same directory, on non-Unix platforms Rename is not an atomic operation.
If there is an error, it will be of type *LinkError.

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `oldpath` | <code>string</code> |
| `newpath` | <code>string</code> |

### $os.remove()

```ts
$os.remove(name: string): void
```

Remove removes the named file or (empty) directory.
If there is an error, it will be of type [*PathError].

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `name` | <code>string</code> |

### $os.removeAll()

```ts
$os.removeAll(path: string): void
```

RemoveAll removes path and any children it contains.
It removes everything it can but returns the first error
it encounters. If the path does not exist, RemoveAll
returns nil (no error).
If there is an error, it will be of type [*PathError].

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `path` | <code>string</code> |

### $os.openRoot()

```ts
$os.openRoot(name: string): (Root)
```

OpenRoot opens the named directory.
It follows symbolic links in the directory name.
If there is an error, it will be of type [*PathError].

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `name` | <code>string</code> |

Returns <code>(<a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/os#osroot">Root</a>)</code>.

### $os.openInRoot()

```ts
$os.openInRoot(dir: string, name: string): (File)
```

OpenInRoot opens the file name in the directory dir.
It is equivalent to OpenRoot(dir) followed by opening the file in the root.

OpenInRoot returns an error if any component of the name
references a location outside of dir.

See [`Root`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/os#osroot) for details and limitations.

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `dir` | <code>string</code> |
| `name` | <code>string</code> |

Returns <code>(<a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/os#osfile">File</a>)</code>.

## $apis

`$apis` defines commonly used PocketBase api helpers and middlewares.

### $apis.static()

```ts
$apis.static(dirOrFS: string|fs.FS, indexFallback: boolean): (e: core.RequestEvent) => void
```

Route handler to serve static directory content (html, js, css, etc.).

If a file resource is missing and indexFallback is true, the request
will be forwarded to the base index.html (useful for SPA with pretty urls).

NB! Expects the route to have a "{path...}" wildcard parameter.

Special redirects:

- if "path" is a file that ends in index.html, it is redirected to its non-index.html version (eg. /test/index.html -> /test/)
- if "path" is a directory that has index.html, the index.html file is rendered,
  otherwise if missing - returns 404 or fallback to the root index.html if indexFallback is true

Example:

```js
// serves static files from the provided dir string path (it will be wrapped in $os.dirFS())
routerAdd("GET", "/{path...}", $apis.static("/path/to/public", false))

// serves static files from the explicit fs.FS value ($os.dirFS(), $os.openRoot().fs(), etc.)
routerAdd("GET", "/{path...}", $apis.static($os.dirFS("/path/to/public"), false))
```

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `dirOrFS` | <code>string&#124;<a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/fs#fsfs">fs.FS</a></code> |
| `indexFallback` | <code>boolean</code> |

Returns <code>(e: <a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/core/events#corerequestevent">core.RequestEvent</a>) =&gt; void</code>.

### $apis.requireGuestOnly()

```ts
$apis.requireGuestOnly(): (hook.Handler<core.RequestEvent | undefined>)
```

RequireGuestOnly middleware requires a request to NOT have a valid
Authorization header.

This middleware is the opposite of [apis.RequireAuth()].

Returns <code>(<a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/hook#hookhandler">hook.Handler</a>&lt;<a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/core/events#corerequestevent">core.RequestEvent</a> &#124; undefined&gt;)</code>.

### $apis.requireAuth()

```ts
$apis.requireAuth(...optCollectionNames: string[]): (hook.Handler<core.RequestEvent | undefined>)
```

RequireAuth middleware requires a request to have a valid record Authorization header.

The auth record could be from any collection.
You can further filter the allowed record auth collections by specifying their names.

Example:

```
	apis.RequireAuth()                      // any auth collection
	apis.RequireAuth("_superusers", "users") // only the listed auth collections
```

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `...optCollectionNames` | <code>string[]</code> (optional) |

Returns <code>(<a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/hook#hookhandler">hook.Handler</a>&lt;<a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/core/events#corerequestevent">core.RequestEvent</a> &#124; undefined&gt;)</code>.

### $apis.requireSuperuserAuth()

```ts
$apis.requireSuperuserAuth(): (hook.Handler<core.RequestEvent | undefined>)
```

RequireSuperuserAuth middleware requires a request to have
a valid superuser Authorization header.

Returns <code>(<a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/hook#hookhandler">hook.Handler</a>&lt;<a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/core/events#corerequestevent">core.RequestEvent</a> &#124; undefined&gt;)</code>.

### $apis.requireSuperuserOrOwnerAuth()

```ts
$apis.requireSuperuserOrOwnerAuth(ownerIdPathParam: string): (hook.Handler<core.RequestEvent | undefined>)
```

RequireSuperuserOrOwnerAuth middleware requires a request to have
a valid superuser or regular record owner Authorization header set.

This middleware is similar to [apis.RequireAuth()] but
for the auth record token expects to have the same id as the path
parameter ownerIdPathParam (default to "id" if empty).

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `ownerIdPathParam` | <code>string</code> |

Returns <code>(<a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/hook#hookhandler">hook.Handler</a>&lt;<a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/core/events#corerequestevent">core.RequestEvent</a> &#124; undefined&gt;)</code>.

### $apis.skipSuccessActivityLog()

```ts
$apis.skipSuccessActivityLog(): (hook.Handler<core.RequestEvent | undefined>)
```

SkipSuccessActivityLog is a helper middleware that instructs the global
activity logger to log only requests that have failed/returned an error.

Returns <code>(<a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/hook#hookhandler">hook.Handler</a>&lt;<a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/core/events#corerequestevent">core.RequestEvent</a> &#124; undefined&gt;)</code>.

### $apis.gzip()

```ts
$apis.gzip(): (hook.Handler<core.RequestEvent | undefined>)
```

Gzip returns a middleware which compresses HTTP response using Gzip compression scheme.

Returns <code>(<a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/hook#hookhandler">hook.Handler</a>&lt;<a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/core/events#corerequestevent">core.RequestEvent</a> &#124; undefined&gt;)</code>.

### $apis.bodyLimit()

```ts
$apis.bodyLimit(limitBytes: number): (hook.Handler<core.RequestEvent | undefined>)
```

BodyLimit returns a middleware handler that changes the default request body size limit.

If limitBytes <= 0, no limit is applied.

Otherwise, if the request body size exceeds the configured limitBytes,
it sends 413 error response.

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `limitBytes` | <code>number</code> |

Returns <code>(<a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/hook#hookhandler">hook.Handler</a>&lt;<a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/core/events#corerequestevent">core.RequestEvent</a> &#124; undefined&gt;)</code>.

### $apis.enrichRecord()

```ts
$apis.enrichRecord(e: core.RequestEvent, record: core.Record, ...defaultExpands: string[]): void
```

EnrichRecord parses the request context and enrich the provided record:
```
  - expands relations (if defaultExpands and/or ?expand query param is set)
  - ensures that the emails of the auth record and its expanded auth relations
    are visible only for the current logged superuser, record owner or record with manage access
```

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `e` | <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/core/events#corerequestevent">core.RequestEvent</a></code> |
| `record` | <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/core/records#corerecord">core.Record</a></code> |
| `...defaultExpands` | <code>string[]</code> (optional) |

### $apis.enrichRecords()

```ts
$apis.enrichRecords(e: core.RequestEvent, records: Array<(core.Record | undefined)>, ...defaultExpands: string[]): void
```

EnrichRecords parses the request context and enriches the provided records:
```
  - expands relations (if defaultExpands and/or ?expand query param is set)
  - ensures that the emails of the auth records and their expanded auth relations
    are visible only for the current logged superuser, record owner or record with manage access
```

Note: Expects all records to be from the same collection!

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `e` | <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/core/events#corerequestevent">core.RequestEvent</a></code> |
| `records` | <code>Array&lt;(<a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/core/records#corerecord">core.Record</a> &#124; undefined)&gt;</code> |
| `...defaultExpands` | <code>string[]</code> (optional) |

### $apis.recordAuthResponse()

```ts
$apis.recordAuthResponse(e: core.RequestEvent, authRecord: core.Record, authMethod: string, meta?: any): void
```

RecordAuthResponse writes standardized json record auth response
into the specified request event.

The authMethod argument specify the name of the current authentication method (eg. password, oauth2, etc.)
that it is used primarily as an auth identifier during MFA and for login alerts.

Set authMethod to empty string if you want to ignore the MFA checks and the login alerts
(can be also adjusted additionally via the onRecordAuthRequest hook).

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `e` | <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/core/events#corerequestevent">core.RequestEvent</a></code> |
| `authRecord` | <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/core/records#corerecord">core.Record</a></code> |
| `authMethod` | <code>string</code> |
| `meta` | <code>any</code> (optional) |

## $http

`$http` defines common methods for working with HTTP requests.

### $http.send()

```ts
$http.send(config: { url: string, body?: string|FormData, method?: string, // default to "GET" headers?: { [key:string]: string }, timeout?: number, // default to 120 // @deprecated please use body instead data?: { [key:string]: any }, }): { statusCode: number, headers: { [key:string]: Array<string> }, cookies: { [key:string]: http.Cookie }, json: any, body: Array<number>, // @deprecated please use toString(result.body) instead raw: string, }
```

Sends a single HTTP request.

Example:

```js
const res = $http.send({
    method:  "POST",
    url:     "https://example.com",
    body:    JSON.stringify({"title": "test"}),
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }
})

console.log(res.statusCode) // the response HTTP status code
console.log(res.headers)    // the response headers (eg. res.headers['X-Custom'][0])
console.log(res.cookies)    // the response cookies (eg. res.cookies.sessionId.value)
console.log(res.body)       // the response body as raw bytes slice
console.log(res.json)       // the response body as parsed json array or map
```

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `config` | <code>{ url: string, body?: string&#124;<a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase#formdata">FormData</a>, method?: string, // default to &#34;GET&#34; headers?: { [key:string]: string }, timeout?: number, // default to 120 // @deprecated please use body instead data?: { [key:string]: any }, }</code> |

Returns <code>{ statusCode: number, headers: { [key:string]: Array&lt;string&gt; }, cookies: { [key:string]: <a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/http#httpcookie">http.Cookie</a> }, json: any, body: Array&lt;number&gt;, // @deprecated please use toString(result.body) instead raw: string, }</code>.

## Functions

### cronAdd()

```ts
cronAdd(jobId: string, cronExpr: string, handler: () => void): void
```

CronAdd registers a new cron job.

If a cron job with the specified name already exist, it will be
replaced with the new one.

Example:

```js
// prints "Hello world!" on every 30 minutes
cronAdd("hello", "*\/30 * * * *", () => {
    console.log("Hello world!")
})
```

_Note that this method is available only in pb_hooks context._

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `jobId` | <code>string</code> |
| `cronExpr` | <code>string</code> |
| `handler` | <code>() =&gt; void</code> |

### cronRemove()

```ts
cronRemove(jobId: string): void
```

CronRemove removes a single registered cron job by its name.

Example:

```js
cronRemove("hello")
```

_Note that this method is available only in pb_hooks context._

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `jobId` | <code>string</code> |

### routerAdd()

```ts
routerAdd(method: string, path: string, handler: (e: core.RequestEvent) => void, ...middlewares: Array<string|((e: core.RequestEvent) => void)|Middleware>): void
```

RouterAdd registers a new route definition.

Example:

```js
routerAdd("GET", "/hello", (e) => {
    return e.json(200, {"message": "Hello!"})
}, $apis.requireAuth())
```

_Note that this method is available only in pb_hooks context._

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `method` | <code>string</code> |
| `path` | <code>string</code> |
| `handler` | <code>(e: <a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/core/events#corerequestevent">core.RequestEvent</a>) =&gt; void</code> |
| `...middlewares` | <code>Array&lt;string&#124;((e: <a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/core/events#corerequestevent">core.RequestEvent</a>) =&gt; void)&#124;Middleware&gt;</code> (optional) |

### routerUse()

```ts
routerUse(...middlewares: Array<string|((e: core.RequestEvent) => void)|Middleware>): void
```

RouterUse registers one or more global middlewares that are executed
along the handler middlewares after a matching route is found.

Example:

```js
routerUse((e) => {
  console.log(e.request.url.path)
  return e.next()
})
```

_Note that this method is available only in pb_hooks context._

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `...middlewares` | <code>Array&lt;string&#124;((e: <a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/core/events#corerequestevent">core.RequestEvent</a>) =&gt; void)&#124;Middleware&gt;</code> (optional) |

### readerToString()

```ts
readerToString(reader: any, maxBytes?: number): string
```

This method is superseded by toString.

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `reader` | <code>any</code> |
| `maxBytes` | <code>number</code> (optional) |

Returns <code>string</code>.

### toString()

```ts
toString(val: any, maxBytes?: number): string
```

toString stringifies the specified value.

Support optional second maxBytes argument to limit the max read bytes
when the value is a io.Reader (default to 32MB).

Types that don't have explicit string representation are json serialized.

Example:

```js
// io.Reader
const ex1 = toString(e.request.body)

// slice of bytes
const ex2 = toString([104 101 108 108 111]) // "hello"

// null
const ex3 = toString(null) // ""
```

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `val` | <code>any</code> |
| `maxBytes` | <code>number</code> (optional) |

Returns <code>string</code>.

### toBytes()

```ts
toBytes(val: any, maxBytes?: number): Array<number>
```

toBytes converts the specified value into a bytes slice.

Support optional second maxBytes argument to limit the max read bytes
when the value is a io.Reader (default to 32MB).

Types that don't have Go slice representation (bool, objects, etc.)
are serialized to UTF8 string and its bytes slice is returned.

Example:

```js
// io.Reader
const ex1 = toBytes(e.request.body)

// string
const ex2 = toBytes("hello") // [104 101 108 108 111]

// object (the same as the string '{"test":1}')
const ex3 = toBytes({"test":1}) // [123 34 116 101 115 116 34 58 49 125]

// null
const ex4 = toBytes(null) // []
```

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `val` | <code>any</code> |
| `maxBytes` | <code>number</code> (optional) |

Returns <code>Array&lt;number&gt;</code>.

### sleep()

```ts
sleep(milliseconds: number): void
```

sleep pauses the current goroutine for at least the specified user duration (in ms).
A zero or negative duration returns immediately.

Example:

```js
sleep(250) // sleeps for 250ms
```

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `milliseconds` | <code>number</code> |

### arrayOf()

```ts
arrayOf(model: T): Array<T>
```

arrayOf creates a placeholder array of the specified models.
Usually used to populate DB result into an array of models.

Example:

```js
const records = arrayOf(new Record)

$app.recordQuery("articles").limit(10).all(records)
```

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `model` | <code>T</code> |

Returns <code>Array&lt;T&gt;</code>.

### unmarshal()

```ts
unmarshal(data: any, dst: any): void
```

unmarshal clones and merges the data argument on top of dst.

This method is rarely used directly by the users and it is most
commonly used in the autogenerated migrations.

To an extent it is similar to the JS native `Object.assign`
but the arguments are reversed and it invokes the Go standard
`json.Marshal/Unmarshal` methods under the hood.

The data argument could be anything serializable, usually a plain object (map).
The dst argument could be any pointer value, usually a model instance.

Example:

```js
unmarshal({ authAlert: { enabled: true } }, collection)
```

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `data` | <code>any</code> |
| `dst` | <code>any</code> |


### setTimeout()

```ts
setTimeout(callback: (...args: A) => void, ms?: number, ...args: A): number
```

Runs `callback(...args)` once after `ms` milliseconds (at least 1), as its own task. A timer set while a request is
served is cleared once the request is answered or its client goes away; one set at the top of a file runs until
cleared. Returns the id for `clearTimeout`.

```js
const word = await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 500, "later"))
```

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `callback` | <code>(...args: A) =&gt; void</code> |
| `ms` | <code>number</code> (optional) |
| `...args` | <code>A</code> (optional) |

Returns <code>number</code>.

### setInterval()

```ts
setInterval(callback: (...args: A) => void, ms?: number, ...args: A): number
```

Runs `callback(...args)` every `ms` milliseconds (at least 1); the next run is timed from the end of the last one.
Cleared like `setTimeout`. Returns the id for `clearInterval`.

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `callback` | <code>(...args: A) =&gt; void</code> |
| `ms` | <code>number</code> (optional) |
| `...args` | <code>A</code> (optional) |

Returns <code>number</code>.

### clearTimeout()

```ts
clearTimeout(id: number | undefined | null): void
```

Cancels a `setTimeout` (an unknown id does nothing). @group PocketOne

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `id` | <code>number &#124; undefined &#124; null</code> |

### clearInterval()

```ts
clearInterval(id: number | undefined | null): void
```

Cancels a `setInterval` (an unknown id does nothing). @group PocketOne

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `id` | <code>number &#124; undefined &#124; null</code> |

### queueMicrotask()

```ts
queueMicrotask(callback: () => void): void
```

Runs `callback` after the current task, before any timer. @group PocketOne

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `callback` | <code>() =&gt; void</code> |

### require()

```ts
require(id: string): any
```

Loads a CommonJS module (`.js`, `.cjs`, `.cts`, `.json`, a `node_modules` package) or an ES module without top-level
await (`.mjs`, `.ts`, `.mts`), relative to the calling file. A module loads once per app.

| Parameter | Type |
|---|---|
| `id` | <code>string</code> |

Returns <code>any</code>.

## Classes

### DynamicModel

```ts
new (shape?: { [key:string]: any })
```

DynamicModel creates a new dynamic model with fields from the provided data shape.

Caveats:
- In order to use 0 as double/float initialization number you have to negate it (`-0`).
- You need to use lowerCamelCase when accessing the model fields (e.g. `model.roles` and not `model.Roles` even if in the model shape and in the DB table the column is capitalized).
- Objects are loaded into types.JSONMap, meaning that they need to be accessed with `get(key)` (e.g. `model.meta.get('something')`).
- For describing nullable types you can use the `null*()` helpers - `nullString()`, `nullInt()`, `nullFloat()`, `nullBool()`, `nullArray()`, `nullObject()`.

Example:

```js
const model = new DynamicModel({
    name:       ""     // or nullString() if nullable
    age:        0,     // or nullInt() if nullable
    totalSpent: -0,    // or nullFloat() if nullable
    active:     false, // or nullBool() if nullable
    Roles:      [],    // or nullArray() if nullable; maps to "Roles" in the DB/JSON but the prop would be accessible via "model.roles"
    meta:       {},    // or nullObject() if nullable
})
```

### Context

```ts
new (parentCtx?: Context, key?: any, value?: any)
```

Context creates a new empty Go context.Context.

This is usually used as part of some Go transitive bindings.

Example:

```js
const blank = new Context()

// with single key-value pair
const base = new Context(null, "a", 123)
console.log(base.value("a")) // 123

// extend with additional key-value pair
const sub = new Context(base, "b", 456)
console.log(sub.value("a")) // 123
console.log(sub.value("b")) // 456
```

Is a <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/context#contextcontext">context.Context</a></code>.

### Record

```ts
new (collection?: core.Collection, data?: { [key:string]: any })
```

Record model class.

```js
const collection = $app.findCollectionByNameOrId("article")

const record = new Record(collection, {
    title: "Lorem ipsum"
})

// or set field values after the initialization
record.set("description", "...")
```

Is a <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/core/records#corerecord">core.Record</a></code>.

### Collection

```js
const collection = new Collection({
    type:       "base",

    listRule:   "@request.auth.id != '' || status = 'public'",
    viewRule:   "@request.auth.id != '' || status = 'public'",
    deleteRule: "@request.auth.id != ''",
    fields: [
        {
            name: "title",
            type: "text",
            required: true,
            min: 6,
            max: 100,
        },
        {
            name: "description",
            type: "text",
        },
    ]
})
```

Is a <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/core/records#corecollection">core.Collection</a></code>.

### MailerMessage

```ts
new (message?: Partial<mailer.Message>)
```

MailerMessage defines a single email message.

```js
const message = new MailerMessage({
    from: {
        address: $app.settings().meta.senderAddress,
        name:    $app.settings().meta.senderName,
    },
    to:      [{address: "test@example.com"}],
    subject: "YOUR_SUBJECT...",
    html:    "YOUR_HTML_BODY...",
})

$app.newMailClient().send(message)
```

Is a <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/mailer#mailermessage">mailer.Message</a></code>.

### Command

```ts
new (cmd?: Partial<cobra.Command>)
```

Command defines a single console command.

Example:

```js
const command = new Command({
    use: "hello",
    run: (cmd, args) => { console.log("Hello world!") },
})

$app.rootCmd.addCommand(command);
```

Is a <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/cobra#cobracommand">cobra.Command</a></code>.

### RequestInfo

```ts
new (info?: Partial<core.RequestInfo>)
```

RequestInfo defines a single core.RequestInfo instance, usually used
as part of various filter checks.

Example:

```js
const authRecord = $app.findAuthRecordByEmail("users", "test@example.com")

const info = new RequestInfo({
    auth:    authRecord,
    body:    {"name": 123},
    headers: {"x-token": "..."},
})

const record = $app.findFirstRecordByData("articles", "slug", "hello")

const canAccess = $app.canAccessRecord(record, info, "@request.auth.id != '' && @request.body.name = 123")
```

Is a <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/core#corerequestinfo">core.RequestInfo</a></code>.

### Middleware

Middleware defines a single request middleware handler.

This class is usually used when you want to explicitly specify a priority to your custom route middleware.

Example:

```js
routerUse(new Middleware((e) => {
  console.log(e.request.url.path)
  return e.next()
}, -10))
```

### Timezone

```ts
new (name?: string)
```

Timezone returns the timezone location with the given name.

The name is expected to be a location name corresponding to a file
in the IANA Time Zone database, such as "America/New_York".

If the name is "Local", LoadLocation returns Local.

If the name is "", invalid or "UTC", returns UTC.

The constructor is equivalent to calling the Go `time.LoadLocation(name)` method.

Example:

```js
const zone = new Timezone("America/New_York")
$app.cron().setTimezone(zone)
```

Is a <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/time#timelocation">time.Location</a></code>.

### DateTime

```ts
new (date?: string, defaultParseInLocation?: string)
```

DateTime defines a single DateTime type instance.
The returned date is always represented in UTC.

Example:

```js
const dt0 = new DateTime() // now

// full datetime string
const dt1 = new DateTime('2023-07-01 00:00:00.000Z')

// datetime string with default "parse in" timezone location
//
// similar to new DateTime('2023-07-01 00:00:00 +01:00') or new DateTime('2023-07-01 00:00:00 +02:00')
// but accounts for the daylight saving time (DST)
const dt2 = new DateTime('2023-07-01 00:00:00', 'Europe/Amsterdam')
```

Is a <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/types#typesdatetime">types.DateTime</a></code>.

### ValidationError

```ts
new (code?: string, message?: string)
```

ValidationError defines a single formatted data validation error,
usually used as part of an error response.

```js
new ValidationError("invalid_title", "Title is not valid")
```

Is a <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/ozzo_validation#ozzo_validationerror">ozzo_validation.Error</a></code>.

### Cookie

```ts
new (options?: Partial<http.Cookie>)
```

A Cookie represents an HTTP cookie as sent in the Set-Cookie header of an
HTTP response.

Example:

```js
routerAdd("POST", "/example", (c) => {
    c.setCookie(new Cookie({
        name:     "example_name",
        value:    "example_value",
        path:     "/",
        domain:   "example.com",
        maxAge:   10,
        secure:   true,
        httpOnly: true,
        sameSite: 3,
    }))

    return c.redirect(200, "/");
})
```

Is a <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/http#httpcookie">http.Cookie</a></code>.

### SubscriptionMessage

```ts
new (options?: Partial<subscriptions.Message>)
```

SubscriptionMessage defines a realtime subscription payload.

Example:

```js
onRealtimeConnectRequest((e) => {
    e.client.send(new SubscriptionMessage({
        name: "example",
        data: '{"greeting": "Hello world"}'
    }))
})
```

Is a <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/subscriptions#subscriptionsmessage">subscriptions.Message</a></code>.

### Buffer

## Hooks

Each hook takes a handler that gets the event; call `e.next()` to go on to the next handler (and the action itself). Hooks marked with tags take collection names (or ids) after the handler, so the handler runs only for those.

| Hook | Event | |
|---|---|---|
| `onBackupCreate(handler)` | <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/core/events#corebackupevent">core.BackupEvent</a></code> | OnBackupCreate hook is triggered on each [`App.createBackup`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/core#coreapp) call. |
| `onBackupRestore(handler)` | <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/core/events#corebackupevent">core.BackupEvent</a></code> | OnBackupRestore hook is triggered before app backup restore (aka. [`App.restoreBackup`](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/core#coreapp) call). |
| `onBatchRequest(handler)` | <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/core/events#corebatchrequestevent">core.BatchRequestEvent</a></code> | OnBatchRequest hook is triggered on each API batch request. |
| `onBootstrap(handler)` | <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/core/events#corebootstrapevent">core.BootstrapEvent</a></code> | OnBootstrap hook is triggered when initializing the main application resources (db, app settings, etc). |
| `onBootstrapClear(handler)` | <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/core/events#corebootstrapevent">core.BootstrapEvent</a></code> | OnBootstrapClear hook is triggered when clearing the main application resources (db connections, cron, logger, etc.) |
| `onCollectionAfterCreateError(handler, ...tags)` | <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/core/events#corecollectionerrorevent">core.CollectionErrorEvent</a></code> | OnCollectionAfterCreateError is a Collection proxy model hook of `OnModelAfterCreateError`. |
